Equipment makers pivot to outcome businesses: connected machines, service contracts and uptime guarantees replace box sales. The pivot is an engineering program — fleet connectivity, service intelligence and outcome pricing — built once, monetized for decades.

items: Field service scheduling by phone and spreadsheet; first-time-fix suffers.
Machines in the field lack telemetry; service is reactive and parts planning blind.

Governance inherits the sector frame — EU Machinery Regulation/CRA among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Manufacturing & Industrial level this capability reads as: RUL signals converted into cost-optimal maintenance windows with parts staging (unplanned downtime down 30-50%). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

The cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability, and it does not flex by account. The first quarter of the rhythm is verification: weeks 1–2 measure the current metric with your team and lock it by signature. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with your control owner receiving evidence weekly. Weeks 9–12 industrialize: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and the measured delta against the signed baseline. Gates are binding: miss one and the program stops or redirects with a documented decision.
